text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft this, I need a few answers. Your current investors will check the numbers, and two of them stand out:

- **Runway:** At $95,000 a month, $340,000 lasts about 3.5 months, so you have cash until roughly early March. That's before your March–April sales peak.
- **Profitability:** Your revenue averaged about $35,000 a month, but 70% of it came in two months, so May through August were probably much lower. Burn is $95,000. Saying you'll be profitable next year will only hold up if the update shows how you get there.

My questions, most important first:

1. **What's the route to profitability?** How many hives under sensor next year, what new revenue, any cost cuts, and in which month do you expect to break even? And what does the $600,000 pay for: how many months, and which milestone should it get you to?
2. **What are the bridge terms?** SAFE or convertible note, cap and discount, minimum cheque, close date, and how much is already committed (and by whom, if you can say).
3. **What's your answer to the $45 competitor?** Maybe better detection, the app, your relationships with beekeepers, or something else. Has any customer left, stalled or asked for a lower price since May?
4. **What evidence goes beyond the one customer?** For example: total hives running sensors, how many of the 31 have renewed or added hives, monthly app revenue, or any comparison of hives with and without sensors in the same operation. Can I name the 4,000-hive customer, and can I quote him?
5. **Who reads it and who signs it?** How many investors, how they invested (angels or funds), and who signs. Did your last update promise anything they'll remember, like a customer target or a revenue figure?
6. **What will they learn anyway?** Is there a cost, a missed target, a weak number or a setback I haven't heard about? For instance: revenue since May, a key hire leaving, or production problems.

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write without them rather than guess.

1. I don't have a break-even month or hive projections. Honestly I can't promise profit next year, you're right. Write a claim the numbers support instead. On costs: I can get spending down to $75,000 a month by February by not filling two open roles. I don't have a milestone plan for the $600k beyond that.

2. Convertible note, 20% discount, $6 million cap. Closes December 15. One angel has already committed $250,000. Don't know about a minimum cheque. Investors who want in should reply to me by December 1.

3. Their sensor only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. No one's left or asked for a lower price that I know of, but three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor.

4. I don't know the total hives, renewals or monthly app revenue offhand. No same-operation comparison. Don't know if I can name or quote him.

5. Company is HiveSense. I don't know the investor count or breakdown off the top of my head. Not sure about promises in the last update.

6. Nothing else I know of. I can commit to a monthly cash report to everyone who puts money into the bridge, if that helps.

**Subject: HiveSense half-year update, and a bridge round we'd like you in**

Hi all,

Here's where HiveSense stands at the half year, and what we're asking of you.

**In short:** We now have 31 paying beekeepers, up from 12 a year ago. We're raising a $600,000 bridge on a convertible note and want our current investors in it. If you'd like to join, please reply by December 1.

**What went well**

- **Customers:** 31 commercial beekeepers are paying us, compared with 12 a year ago.
- **Revenue:** $212,000 for the half.
- **Unit economics:** Each sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55. On top of that, the app brings in $4 a month for every hive, for as long as the hive stays connected.
- **Our largest customer:** He runs 4,000 hives. Last winter he lost 18% of his colonies, against 31% the winter before. He also changed his mite treatment in that time, so we can't claim the whole improvement. He does count our sensors as part of it.

**What you should know**

- **Our revenue is seasonal.** 70% of the half's revenue came in March and April, when beekeepers get ready for pollination. Summer and autumn are thin, and most of next year's revenue will come in spring.
- **Cash.** We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 in the bank. Without new money, we run out around the end of March 2027. That is the middle of the season that brings in most of our revenue.
- **Competition.** In May, a large farm equipment company launched a hive sensor at $45. Theirs measures only temperature. Ours measures temperature, sound and hive weight. No customer has left us or asked for a lower price. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test the competing sensor, and I'll tell you what they find.

**What we're doing about it**

We're bringing monthly spending down to $75,000 by February by leaving two open roles unfilled.

With that cut and the $600,000 bridge, our cash lasts to about November 2027, and that's before counting any revenue. It carries us through the whole 2027 spring season and leaves time afterwards to show what that season produced.

I'm not going to promise you profit next year, because I don't yet have a break-even plan I'd stand behind. What I can promise is this: everyone who joins the bridge will get a cash report every month, showing what's in the bank, what we spent and what came in. You'll see how we're doing as it happens, not twice a year.

**The terms**

- Convertible note: 20% discount, $6 million cap
- $250,000 already committed by one angel, so $350,000 is still open
- Please tell me by December 1 if you want in
- The round closes December 15

If you'd like to join, reply with the amount you're considering by December 1. If you have questions about the competing sensor, the seasonality or anything else, I'd rather hear them now than after the round closes.

Thank you for backing us this far.

[Your name]
HiveSense
</final_document>

I couldn't make "profitable next year" stand up, so the update makes a smaller claim the numbers do support. With $600,000 more and spending cut to $75,000 a month, the money lasts through the 2027 season even with no new revenue.

- **How I got the runway figures:** I assumed the $340,000 is what you have today, that you spend $95,000 in each of December and January, and $75,000 a month from February. Without the bridge, the money runs out around the end of March. With it, it lasts to about November 2027. Please check these against your own books before you send.
- **What I left out:**
  - The big customer isn't named, since you don't know yet whether you can name him.
  - There's no minimum cheque.
  - Nothing refers to promises from your last update.
- **Worth adding if you can get them quickly:** total hives with sensors and monthly app revenue. They would show investors how much of your income repeats every month, which matters a lot given how seasonal sales are.
- **Things to fill in:** the greeting and your name at the bottom.

It's about 480 words.
